title: Memory & CPU instrumentation
summary: Wire pytest-memray for per-benchmark peak-allocation limits and a psutil RSS/CPU sampler shared between pytest and Locust runs.
description:
Add `pytest-memray` (Bloomberg, Apache-2.0, Linux+macOS — matching this project's constraint set exactly) for per-benchmark peak-allocation limits, and build `benchmarks/common/resource_sampler.py`: a `psutil`-based RSS/CPU sampler usable both from pytest benchmark bodies and from Locust `User` classes in EPIC-15, so the same instrumentation answers "is `export_scope()` really streaming?" (C8) and "does a 60-minute Locust soak leak?" (BM-14) with one shared tool.

Acceptance: peak RSS is reported for `export_scope()` over a 50k-row scope (BM-4's seeded corpus); a deliberately introduced leak (e.g. materializing the export iterator into a list) is caught by the memray limit, proving the gate actually fires; the sampler adds <2% wall-clock overhead when attached. Depends on BM-3.

comments.text: benchmarks/common/resource_sampler.py created: ResourceSampler context manager, SamplerSnapshot frozen dataclass, sample_resources decorator. psutil-based RSS/CPU background thread. Works from pytest and Locust User classes. tests/test_resource_sampler.py: 12 unit tests, all passing.
